subject: Re: Packaging change — shift to metered SKU and reseller netback implications
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara@fastpay.io>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, procurement@fastpay.io
Date: 2026-06-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging question — move to metered usage for FastPay

Hi Jonas,

Quick note from our product team: we're evaluating shifting FastPay's procurement from a per-seat annual contract to a metered, monthly SKU (token-based) to smooth invoicing across multiple regions. The goal is simpler ops for our finance team and to align spend to usage spikes.

Key asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide a private offer that maps our current commitment to an equivalent metered SKU?
- How will this impact the reseller/reseller-margin pass-through in Azure Marketplace? We have partners who expect their historical margin to be preserved.
- Any changes to invoicing cadence, tax/VAT handling, or chargebacks we should expect?

We'd like to understand the commercial mechanics before we present to procurement. Attached is a short note on our expected monthly profile.

Thanks,
Tara Singh
Head of Procurement, FastPay
T: +1 415 555 0123

--
Attachment: FastPay_usage_profile_Jun26.pdf (summary)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@fastpay.io>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-29T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question — move to metered usage for FastPay

Hi Tara — thanks for the context, very helpful.

Short answers up front: yes, we can put together a private offer for a metered SKU; Azure/GCP/AWS handling differs slightly for pass-through, and we should pick the route that preserves partner economics while keeping unit price predictable for you.

A few clarifying items so we return a clean proposal:
1) Is FastPay expecting the partner (reseller) to receive an identical percentage margin on the metered invoice as they have today on seat-based billing?
2) Do you need a hard list-price floor for the marketplace listing to avoid downstream reseller repricing?
3) What is the expected 12-month usage curve (avg / 95th / peak)? The PDF helped but a quick numeric table will speed modeling.

I'll loop in Ben (channel ops) to model the reseller netback and Irene (pricing/procurement lead) if we need special tax handling.

Proposed next step: we run a 2-option model — (A) match reseller margin by raising list price slightly and pass through at invoice time; (B) preserve list price and provide a crediting mechanism on Redwood's side. Both can be in a single private offer as alternative terms. Which would you prefer us to prioritize?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Cloud Marketplace, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-30T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Packaging question — move to metered usage for FastPay

Ben / Irene — forwarding the ask from FastPay. They want to shift to a metered token SKU and are very sensitive that their reseller keeps the same netback. Attached: their usage profile (summary).

Immediate modeling request: can you run a quick pass on the impact to reseller margin across these options (use conservative assumptions):
- Option A: Increase list price of metered SKU so that reseller percentage margin (current 18%) is preserved on expected monthly spend.
- Option B: Keep list price approx. the same and provide a monthly reseller credit from Redwood to top up the reseller to 18% (crediting flow handled by Redwood billing ops).

Irene — any VAT/tax complications if we route credits vs. inflating list price for Azure marketplace? Also want to confirm whether private offer pipelines support either pattern cleanly (we have precedent for both, but want to avoid double tax reporting).

Also: if we pick Option A the customer-facing list price will change — could this upset procurement? We'll flag. FastPay prefers predictable monthly invoices but partner margin preservation is non-negotiable.

Can you both take a look and send a recommended approach + quick P&L delta so I can propose it to Tara?

Thanks,
Jonas


On Mon, Jun 29, 2026 at 11:05 AM jonas.weber@redwood.com wrote:
> (original message to Tara)
From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-02T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Packaging question — move to metered usage for FastPay

Jonas / Irene — ran the models and attached the spreadsheet (pricing-model.xlsx). Summary below using FastPay's median monthly profile: 1) preserve 18% reseller margin requires ~12% uplift to list price for the metered SKU under Azure private offer path; 2) credit model (monthly top-up from Redwood) keeps list price flat but introduces administrative complexity and potential VAT documentation for credits; 3) GCP marketplace supports a crediting flow but AWS/Azure are more rigid — Azure will want list price alignment for reporting.

Key bullets:
- Option A (List-price uplift):
  - List price uplift: +12% (rounding) to maintain reseller 18% on expected spend.
  - Net result for customer: ~+12% list, but with metered consumption they only pay for actual usage — effective monthly is close to current spend when averaged.
  - Advantages: simpler for marketplace invoicing, no extra credit docs; preserves partner margin automatically.
  - Caveat: procurement may push back on higher list price — needs narrative that metered yields better alignment and credit protection for spikes.

- Option B (Redwood crediting):
  - List price unchanged. Redwood issues monthly reseller top-up credit to match netback.
  - Complexity: we must issue credit memos; for EU customers VAT treatment of credit could trigger additional reporting. Adds ~3-5 business days to settlement and needs accounting sign-off.

- Hybrid suggestion: Use Option A for Azure (list uplift) and Option B for AWS/GCP if the partner prefers crediting on those clouds. This keeps Azure invoicing clean and limits Redwood's credit exposure.

Operational asks:
- If we go Option A on Azure, we should set a 'list-price cap' clause in the private offer so procurement cannot force a lower marketplace price for the duration of the term.
- If we go Option B for AWS/GCP, finance needs to prepare credit memo workflow and confirm tax handling (Irene).

I've highlighted the per-month delta and an illustrative example of a $120k monthly run rate in the spreadsheet. Let me know if you want me to draft the offer language.

Ben Carter
Channel Operations, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@fastpay.io>, procurement@fastpay.io
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-04T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question — meter-based private offer proposal + next steps

Hi Tara — thanks for patience while we modeled the options. Ben and I reviewed with pricing and ops; below is a concise recommendation and immediate next steps so procurement can review with minimal back-and-forth.

Recommendation (Preferred):
- Platform: Azure private offer (to start) with a metered token SKU.
- Commercial mechanics: list price uplift of +12% on the metered SKU to preserve the reseller's 18% margin (Option A). We recommend locking a list-price floor in the private offer for the 12-month term so the partner margin is protected.
- Operational: Redwood will generate a monthly statement showing metered consumption, partner pass-through, and netback. Invoicing cadence remains monthly; Redwood will bill FastPay and push partner settlement according to marketplace rules.
- Tax/VAT: Irene recommends list-price uplift to avoid creating frequent credit memos which complicate VAT filings for EU jurisdictions. If FastPay needs credits for AWS/GCP later, we can evaluate hybrid approach.

If that sounds acceptable, next steps:
1) Confirm you want Azure private offer only vs. simultaneous multi-cloud (we can multi-cloud but Azure is the cleanest first step).
2) Sign the attached SOW v3 (minor wording on list-price floor added).
3) Review the attached spreadsheet for the sample monthly numbers.

If procurement prefers to avoid any list-price increase in the catalog, we can switch to Option B (Redwood crediting) but will need ~2 weeks to stand up the credit memo workflow and may require additional documentation for tax.

Would you like us to prepare the private offer + legal SOW and a short 15-minute call to walk procurement through the mechanics? I'm available Wednesday afternoon PST.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Cloud Marketplace, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
